A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the CLLMate/WCEF research project using ERA5 meteorology and news-derived events. Although v2 substantially reframes the work, the main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments and component ablations in Tables 1–2, plus qualitative model comparisons in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original model benchmarking in Table 2, ablations in Table 3, expert annotation agreement in Appendix B.2, and case studies in Appendix D.

M1.justification: v1 proposes a Llama3-8B model with knowledge-graph pretraining, trainable raster encoding/projection, and LoRA tuning. v2 removes that model and graph-training stage, benchmarking existing MLLMs and fine-tuning LLaVA with frozen vision encoders/adapters instead. Dataset construction also changes from Llama3-70B extraction and geopy filtering to GPT-4o-mini extraction, expert validation, regional alignment, and hierarchical categorization.

E1.justification: The ERA5 and Wisers sources remain, but coverage expands from China to 1,049 regions distributed globally. Evaluation changes from generating daily event lists for China to selecting hierarchical categories for individual regional meteorological phenomena and consequences. These are substantive changes in geographic coverage and task requirements.

E2.justification: v1 quantitatively compares CLLMate with top-1 similarity and LLaVA-based tuning, with additional MLLMs appearing in qualitative cases. v2 removes top-1 similarity and evaluates random/majority guessing alongside 23 model variants. Table 2 includes newly evaluated comparators such as Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Janus-Pro, Cambrian, and Qwen2.5-VL, plus expanded LLaVA comparisons.

E3.justification: The chronological test allocation changes from approximately 13% to 10%. Text-generation metrics are replaced by classification accuracy at two hierarchical levels. v2 introduces standardized answer codes, randomized option ordering, and structured zero-shot reasoning prompts. Its one-epoch LLaVA fine-tuning experiments replace v1's knowledge pretraining followed by three multimodal tuning epochs.

E4.justification: v1's knowledge-graph, context, and raster ablations are replaced by image, statistics, and zero-shot reasoning ablations on Gemini-2.0-flash and LLaVA-1.6-mistral-7B. Appendix D adds model-scale and architectural comparisons. The original China-wide examples are replaced by detailed Guangzhou heat and California wildfire cases with expert-marked model errors.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 newly reports three annotators, pairwise agreement of 81.83%, and Fleiss's kappa of 0.63, adding statistical assessment of annotation reliability. v1 has no corresponding analysis. Neither version reports repeated model runs, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for forecasting performance.

E6.justification: The original generation results, including CLLMate's BERTScore of 73.56 versus top-1 similarity's 71.37, are removed. v2 reports new classification results, including 45.93% primary-phenomena accuracy for fine-tuned LLaVA-1.5-7B and 16.25% subordinate-consequence accuracy for Qwen2.5-VL-72B, alongside new ablation and case outcomes. These replace results under different tasks and settings; they do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The raster/event definitions and core forecasting Equations 1–2 remain substantively unchanged. v2 removes the knowledge-graph definition and supporting mathematical specifications of the former model, including embedding, training-loss, and nearest-neighbor prediction formulas. Neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: CLLMate changes from a proposed forecasting model claimed to outperform baselines into a dataset and benchmark exposing existing MLLMs' capabilities and limitations. The abstract, contributions, and conclusion drop the original model-superiority and WCRP deployment contributions. The WCEF task proposal remains, but the central contribution and claimed outcome are substantially redefined.

C2.justification: v1 attributes success primarily to knowledge-graph learning and raster-text alignment. v2 instead discusses class imbalance, geographic reporting bias, difficulties predicting consequences, model-dependent modality redundancy, and limits of scaling. Knowledge-graph incorporation becomes future work. Appendix A.4 also distinguishes potential generative applications from the multiple-choice evaluation actually conducted.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C add the dataset schema, annotation and adjudication procedures, detailed forecasting prompts, ERA5 access/license information, and a planned CC BY 4.0 release after review. Fine-tuning documentation specifies frozen components, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, learning rate 2e-5, batch size 16, eight A800 GPUs, and training times. v1 largely referred readers to recommended training hyperparameters; public dataset availability is still only promised in v2.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the extensive instruction-tuning dataset discussion with substantive positioning against meteorological and event datasets. Section 2.3 and Table 1 compare CLLMate with SEVIR, Mesogeos, Digital Typhoon, NeuralNERE, ClimateIQA, and WeatherQA, emphasizing verified event records and downstream impacts. Model and annotation references also change substantially.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around a benchmark contribution. Related work moves before problem formulation, the original methodology narrative becomes dataset construction and benchmarking, and supporting material is reorganized into structured Appendices A–D. These are substantial narrative and organizational changes beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: The framework diagram is revised and resized; the original graph/instruction illustrations and case displays are replaced. v2 adds geographic and temporal distributions, category charts, a taxonomy diagram, a dataset-comparison table, and substantially redesigned performance tables. Appendix scale plots redisplay Table 2 results, while prompts and cases receive new boxed layouts. The document template also changes throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the benchmark's empirical foundation: systematic expert validation and agreement reporting address v1's undocumented label-validation process, while explicit prompts, data schemas, and training settings improve reproducibility. Broader comparisons support more qualified conclusions about model limitations. These gains outweigh the narrower multiple-choice evaluation. A material caveat remains: Section 5.4 selects a majority baseline whose primary category differs from Figure 6's largest training category, weakening that comparison. The improvement concerns benchmark credibility and auditability, not demonstrated gains in open-ended forecasting.
